Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The diagram shows the demand curve for a product. price D O quantity Which statement is correct?

options.A: Consumer expenditure on the product always rises when price falls.
options.B: Demand is less elastic at higher prices than at lower prices.
options.C: Price elasticity of demand differs at every price.
options.D: Price elasticity of demand equals one at every price.

questions.questionText: The cross-elasticity of demand between two goods will be higher

options.A: the greater the difference in price between the two goods.
options.B: the greater the income elasticities of demand for the two goods.
options.C: the greater the price elasticities of demand for the two goods.
options.D: the more they are regarded as similar by consumers.

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of supply of a good is +2. The quantity supplied originally was 200 units. The price increases by 30%. What will the quantity supplied be after the price increase?

options.A: 80 units B 140 units C 260 units D 320 units

When will the price mechanism not function as a system for allocating goods?

options.A: when the government bans advertising
options.B: when the government maintains an effective maximum price
options.C: when there is a limited supply of the good
options.D: when there is a powerful company able to set the market price

questions.questionText: During a certain period, 10000 units of a normal good are sold at a price of US$20. During a later period, 12000 units are sold at a price of US$22. What could explain this change?

options.A: an increase in indirect taxation
options.B: an increase in the cost of raw materials
options.C: an increase in the price of a substitute commodity
options.D: an increase in the productivity of factors of production

questions.questionText: A free market is in disequilibrium with a shortage of a product. As the market moves towards equilibrium, what will happen to the price, the quantity demanded and the quantity supplied? price quantity demanded quantity supplied

options.A: decrease decrease increase
options.B: decrease increase decrease
options.C: increase decrease increase
options.D: increase increase decrease

X S price E Y E P S w w Z D O Q quantity of products What would be the loss of consumer surplus if all foreign trade were banned?

options.A: P XE B P YE E C YXE D ZYE w 1 w 2 1 2 2

questions.questionText: A government wishes to impose a tax on a good so that the producer and not the consumer pays most of the tax. Which type of elasticity would it be best for the good to have to achieve this aim?

options.A: high price elasticity of demand
options.B: low price elasticity of demand
options.C: totally inelastic price elasticity of demand
options.D: unitary price elasticity of demand

What is not an example of a transfer payment?

options.A: pocket money from parents
options.B: private donations to charities
options.C: salary paid to a teacher in a government school
options.D: unemployment benefit

questions.questionText: In 2016–2017 a government spent $135 billion on the health service. The diagram shows the provision of healthcare in that country. S price ($) P D O Q quantity What can we deduce about healthcare provision in the country if it were provided at zero price?

options.A: At price P the benefits to society are maximised.
options.B: It is non-rival in consumption.
options.C: It is unlimited in supply due to government funding.
options.D: It will need rationing as it will be overconsumed.

questions.questionText: A government privatises the telecommunications industry. What is least likely to increase?

options.A: choice of telecommunications services for consumers
options.B: development of new telecommunications products
options.C: employment in the telecommunications industry
options.D: productivity in the supply of telecommunications

questions.questionText: The diagram shows short-run aggregate supply and demand in an economy, where the initial equilibrium is at S. SRAS price level SRAS SRAS T S AD AD AD O real output What is most likely to cause a movement from S to T?

options.A: an increase in consumer expenditure and an increase in productivity
options.B: an increase in consumer expenditure and a reduction in imports
options.C: an increase in education and training and an increase in income tax
options.D: an increase in the exchange rate and a reduction in corporation tax

questions.questionText: A government statistical office measured changes in income from employment, pensions and benefits, then subtracted income tax and welfare contributions and adjusted for inflation. What did the final figure represent?

options.A: changes in nominal income
options.B: changes in nominal net earnings
options.C: changes in real disposable income
options.D: changes in real gross earnings

questions.questionText: The table shows all of the items on the current account of a country’s balance of payments. $ million exports of goods 143 imports of goods 156 exports of services 75 imports of services 72 net transfers +5 What is the value of the current account balance?

options.A: $5m deficit
options.B: $10m deficit
options.C: $13m deficit
options.D: $3m surplus

questions.questionText: Following a long period of depreciation of the US$, both the US and UK monetary authorities raised their domestic interest rate. What will happen to the value of the exchange rate of the US$ in terms of UK£?

options.A: It will fall.
options.B: It will remain unchanged.
options.C: It will rise.
options.D: The outcome is uncertain.

questions.questionText: Country P exports goods and imports goods. Export prices and import prices are set to an index of 100 in year 1. The table shows corresponding prices indices for years 2 and 3. year 2 year 3 export price index 120 132 import price index 110 121 Which statement is correct?

options.A: It is not possible to say how the terms of trade changed without further information.
options.B: The terms of trade improved between years 1 and 2, and improved again between years 2 and 3.
options.C: The terms of trade improved between years 1 and 2, and then remained unchanged between years 2 and 3.
options.D: The terms of trade worsened throughout the whole period.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, MN is the production possibility curve of a country that has a comparative advantage in the production of good Y. M quantity of good X R O N quantity of good Y What might enable the country to consume the quantities of X and Y indicated by point R?

options.A: a reduction in unemployment
options.B: increased specialisation in the production of good X
options.C: increased specialisation in the production of good Y
options.D: more participation in international trade

questions.questionText: What is the difference between a customs union and a free trade area?

options.A: Only the customs union has a common external tariff with the rest of the world.
options.B: Only the customs union requires fixed exchange rates between member countries.
options.C: Only the free trade area needs to eliminate tariffs between member countries.
options.D: Only the free trade area requires freedom of movement for labour and capital between member countries.

questions.questionText: Which statement about trade protection is correct?

options.A: A tariff will result in a greater decrease in demand for an import the lower its price elasticity of demand is.
options.B: Embargoes are only an effective trade barrier against imports in price-elastic demand.
options.C: Export subsidies to domestic firms will prevent the dumping of foreign products in the domestic market.
options.D: Quotas are less effective than tariffs for raising government revenue.

questions.questionText: What is an example of expansionary monetary policy?

options.A: the central bank buying government bonds in the money market
options.B: the central bank causing an appreciation of the country’s foreign exchange rate
options.C: the central bank increasing controls on credit lending
options.D: the central bank increasing the minimum lending rate of interest

questions.questionText: China had a US$155 billion current account surplus in 2012. Which combination of policies might the Chinese Government use to reduce the surplus?

options.A: decrease income tax and raise the value of the Chinese currency, the Yuan
options.B: increase income tax and lower the value of the Chinese currency, the Yuan
options.C: increase subsidies to Chinese firms and reduce income tax
options.D: increase tariffs on imports and increase income tax

questions.questionText: In an economy, prices are rising. The government wishes to limit further increases in prices. Which policies would it be likely to use?

options.A: decrease goods and services (sales) tax and put a quota on cheap imports
options.B: decrease income tax and decrease interest rates
options.C: increase interest rates and decrease government spending
